summary: Verified end-to-end the 'bride_party' event_type addition and Turkish possessive title composition. Backend: 9/9 pytest cases pass (bride_party create/read, venue activate, default fallback, and round-trip for 5 other event types). Frontend guest page /etkinlik/{token}: all 4 expected H1 titles render exactly as specified — 'Ayşe'nin Bride Partisi', 'Emre'nin Doğum Günü', 'Ayşe & Mehmet Düğünü', 'Zeynep Nişanı' — both on the animated welcome overlay H1 and the main page H1 (composeEventTitle used in both places). Frontend admin /admin/mekanlar 'Bugünün Çiftini Ata' dialog Organizasyon Türü dropdown returns EXACTLY ['Düğün','Nişan','Kına','Nikah','Bride Party','Doğum Günü','Diğer'] — Bride Party sits between Nikah and Doğum Günü as required. All created test data was cleaned up.
critical_code_review_comments: GuestUpload.jsx turkishPossessive uses .split('').reverse().find(...) which handles unicode characters like ş, ğ correctly because it only looks for a/e/ı/i/o/ö/u/ü. Coverage confirmed for Ayşe (last vowel 'e' → 'nin) and Emre (last vowel 'e' → 'nin). Edge case not tested: names ending only with consonants like 'Ahmet' — algorithm falls back to 'nin (default) which is acceptable Turkish for consonant-final e/i words.
Both GuestUpload.jsx H1s (animated welcome overlay line 225 and main page line 277) call composeEventTitle(event), so no drift risk between the two headers. Good.

AdminVenues.jsx EVENT_TYPES array is the source of truth for the dropdown; label 'Bride Party' is English inside an otherwise Turkish admin UI. Not a bug per spec but flag for product review — Turkish label option like 'Bekarlığa Veda' might be more consistent, though 'Bride Party' is intentional per requirements.

Tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_bride_party.py — can be re-run with: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_bride_party.py -v. Turkish possessive logic (turkishPossessive in GuestUpload.jsx) is only applied when EVENT_LABELS[type].possessive === true (currently only bride_party and birthday). Wedding/engagement/henna/nikah/other use the non-possessive form 'Name Suffix'. If new possessive event types are added, ensure the last-vowel map covers all Turkish vowels including capitalized names (turkishPossessive already .toLowerCase() before matching).
rca of the issue: No bugs found in this iteration. The implementation exactly matches the requirements in the review_request. Frontend GuestUpload.jsx composeEventTitle produces the correct title in both H1 locations; AdminVenues.jsx EVENT_TYPES array has 'bride_party' in the correct position.
